papers.title: Target Trial Emulation and the TARGET Guideline to Advance Rural and Remote Health Research.
papers.one_line: Proposes the framework and its reporting guideline as the route to causal evidence for rural and remote Australian health services, where randomized trials are impractical and policy currently rests on urban and international evidence.
papers.what_was_done: Rural and remote Australians have poorer outcomes, less timely access and shorter life expectancy than metropolitan residents, and rural health policy still leans on evidence generated in urban or international settings despite decades of investment in service innovation. Randomized trials are hard to run in these settings, which contributes to under-representation in research. The article argues that where trials are not feasible, observational analyses structured by the target trial framework provide a rigorous and pragmatic alternative, and that the framework has not yet been applied to rural contexts despite international uptake. The recently published TARGET reporting guideline is presented as the tool that makes such studies appraisable. The vision offered is a shift from episodic programme evaluation to a continuous learning culture with research embedded in care through ongoing observational analyses, which the article states requires sustained investment in data linkage and analytic capacity, and partnerships with rural communities built on research co-design and respect for data sovereignty.

future_research.gap: The framework has not been applied to rural and remote contexts at all despite growing international adoption.
future_research.quote: Despite growing international adoption, this approach has not been applied to rural contexts.

problems.evidence: The proposal is conditional on infrastructure that does not exist in these settings, and the article names it: sustained investment in data linkages and analytic capacity. Small distributed health systems are exactly where linkage is weakest, so the data-fitness question is unanswerable before the investment and is not posed as a criterion after it.
problems.quote: Realising this vision requires sustained investment in data linkages, analytic capacity and genuine partnerships with rural communities guided by research co‐design and respect for data sovereignty.

problems.evidence: The argument for adopting the framework in a new setting rests on transparent reporting making it rigorous, with the reporting guideline supplying the standard. Rigor is being located in what a study says about itself rather than in any property of the estimate, which is precisely the substitution at issue when the label travels to a domain with no track record.
problems.quote: When transparently reported, target trial emulation provides rural health researchers with a rigorous yet pragmatic bridge between the ideals of RCTs and the realities of small, distributed health systems.

problems.evidence: The setting is small distributed health systems whose under-representation in trials is attributed to the difficulty of running trials there, and the same small numbers constrain an emulation after eligibility restriction and weighting. The article proposes the design without addressing what effective sample remains.
problems.quote: Although randomised controlled trials (RCTs) remain the most rigorous method for establishing causal relationships and informing equitable health policy, they are challenging to conduct in rural settings, contributing to under‐representation in research.

papers.title: Real-World Emulation of Landmark Lung Cancer Trials: A Registry-Based Reconstruction of KN189, KN407, IMpower133, and PACIFIC.
papers.one_line: Emulates four pivotal checkpoint inhibitor trials in 4,015 patients from one German cancer registry under a single framework, reproducing the survival and response benefits, while restricting to performance status 0 to 1 and using registry response assessment that does not correspond to trial criteria.
papers.what_was_done: The Baden-Wurttemberg Cancer Registry was used to emulate KEYNOTE-189, KEYNOTE-407, IMpower133 and PACIFIC, with eligibility, treatment strategies and outcomes aligned to each trial as far as registry constraints allowed. Time zero was systemic therapy initiation for three emulations and completion of chemoradiotherapy for the fourth, and groups were balanced by propensity-score inverse probability weighting. Across 4,015 patients the checkpoint inhibitor arms showed improved survival, with hazard ratios of 0.59 and 0.69 for the two non-small cell emulations and five-year survival of 22.7 against 4.7 percent and 11.8 against 6.6 percent, and objective response rates consistently above the comparator. Five-year survival matched each original trial closely. No power calculation was performed and sample size was whatever the eligibility criteria yielded. Trial-specific variables including adverse events, detailed comorbidities and smoking status were not captured, PD-L1 status was incomplete, and tumor response in the registry relies on clinical documentation rather than standardized radiologic evaluation so it does not fully correspond to the trials' response criteria. Regimens varied across centres in dosing, duration and supportive care, limiting protocol-level comparability. Emulations were restricted to performance status 0 to 1.

future_research.gap: Whether long-term survivors in the registry differ from trial-like populations was outside the scope and has not been analyzed.
future_research.quote: Notably, long-term survivors in our registry did not appear to differ substantially from the overall trial-like populations with regard to their age, ECOG performance status, or metastatic burden, although dedicated analyses were beyond the scope of the present study.

problems.evidence: Agreement is declared on five-year survival and response rates matching the trials, with no scale on which a near match and a clear one differ, and the emulation was restricted to performance status 0 to 1 so that it would resemble the trials. The paper states this restriction means the findings do not represent the real-world population, which is the population the emulation was meant to speak about.
problems.quote: At the same time, because our emulations were intentionally restricted to ECOG 0–1 patients, these findings should not be interpreted as representative of the full real-world population.

problems.evidence: One of the two reported outcomes is measured differently in the two settings being compared: the registry records response from clinical documentation while the trials used standardized radiologic assessment against defined criteria. The response rates are nevertheless reported side by side with the trial values as evidence of agreement.
problems.quote: Third, the tumor response assessment in the registry does not fully correspond to RECIST-defined ORRs and relies on clinical documentation rather than a standardized radiologic evaluation.

problems.evidence: The treatment strategy is a regimen label under which dosing, duration and supportive care vary between centres, and the paper states this may have influenced outcomes and limited protocol-level comparability with the trials. A subgroup difference by chemotherapy backbone, hazard ratios 0.46 against 0.67 in one emulation, shows the variation is not immaterial.
problems.quote: Finally, variation in the systemic therapy regimens—including the dosing, duration, and supportive care—across centers may have influenced the outcomes and limited the strict protocol-level comparability.

problems.evidence: No power calculation was performed and the sample was however many registry patients met trial eligibility, which for one emulation left 467 patients from a population-based registry. The subgroup analyses on which the chemotherapy backbone comparisons rest are described as exploratory for the same reason.
problems.quote: No formal a priori power calculations were performed due to the retrospective, registry-based design. The sample size was determined by the number of patients meeting trial eligibility criteria in the registry.

problems.evidence: Three trial-relevant confounders are named as not systematically captured, adverse events, detailed comorbidities and smoking status, in a lung cancer study where smoking is a primary prognostic factor. Residual confounding is acknowledged as unexcludable with no bias analysis bounding it.
problems.quote: Important trial-specific variables—such as adverse events, detailed comorbidities, and smoking status—were not systematically captured.

papers.title: Supporting complex mental health care and services research today and beyond: a mini-review of real-world evidence strategies and informed approaches.
papers.one_line: Reviews real-world evidence strategies for mental health services research and names the biases specific to these data, underdiagnosis, stigma-related under-recording and differential follow-up, as things a protocol should say how it will address.
papers.what_was_done: Global mental health need is escalating while only about 7 percent of people with mental disorders receive effective treatment, and real-world data covering records, claims, patient-reported outcomes and digital sources remain underused for understanding care delivery. The review surveys recent studies applying artificial intelligence and machine learning to identify study populations, extract unstructured clinical information or predict treatment patterns, and others characterizing trajectories, service use and costs. Two actions are proposed. The first is adopting routine curation, transformation and analysis approaches including target trial emulation for causal inference, argued to matter particularly in mental health where complex treatment pathways, comorbidities and variable adherence obscure causal relationships. The second is improving data systems through standardization, harmonization and interoperability, with recommendations to standardize data entry, align collection with routine care pathways, and run automated checks for completeness. On transparency the review points to the HARPER protocol template, which should clarify how conditions are defined, how exposures and outcomes are operationalized and how mental-health-specific biases will be handled, the ATRAcTR tool for judging data suitability, the TARGET reporting guideline, and registration on a public real-world evidence registry.

future_research.gap: Causal inference approaches including emulation have not been systematically compared across different data environments and care pathways, and existing studies are concentrated in the United States and Europe.
future_research.quote: Future research should expand RWD-based mental health services studies to underrepresented regions, rigorously evaluate and refine AI/ML tools for real-world clinical use, and systematically compare advanced causal inference approaches—such as target trial emulation—across diverse data environments and care pathways.

problems.evidence: Three mental-health-specific measurement failures are named, underdiagnosis, stigma-related under-recording and differential follow-up, and each attaches to the variable that defines the population. The remedy offered is that a protocol should state how they will be addressed, which locates the problem correctly and supplies no method.
problems.quote: Detailed protocols help clarify how mental health conditions are defined, how exposures (e.g., treatments, service use) and outcomes (e.g., symptom change, hospitalization, suicide attempts) are operationalized, and how biases specific to mental health care data—such as underdiagnosis, stigma-related under recording, or differential follow-up—will be addressed.

problems.evidence: The review states that complex treatment pathways and variable adherence are what make causal relationships hard to see in mental health, and offers the framework as the response. Those pathways are the treatment strategies an emulation would have to define, so the difficulty is being named as the reason to apply the method rather than as a problem the method resolves.
problems.quote: The TTE framework is particularly important for mental health, where complex treatment pathways, comorbidities, and variable treatment adherence might obscure causal relationships.

problems.evidence: The second recommended action is to standardize and harmonize data entry and align collection with routine care pathways, which is a call to change how the data are produced rather than a way to work with what exists. In a field where the same diagnostic label is recorded differently across services, harmonizing structure is what is being proposed and semantic equivalence is what would be needed.
problems.quote: Improving mental health-relevant data systems using standardization and harmonization techniques for the purpose of aligning data collection with routine yet complex care pathways is, therefore, a critical action or step moving forward ( 28 ).

papers.title: Target Trial Emulation Meta-Analysis of Benzodiazepines For Out-of-Hospital Status Epilepticus in Adults.
papers.one_line: Uses the target trial framework at the level of a meta-analysis, modeling study design features as covariates in meta-regression to estimate what benzodiazepine efficacy would be under an ideal double-blind randomized trial, and finds conventional pooling overstates it by 3.9 percentage points.
papers.what_was_done: Reported seizure cessation rates for benzodiazepines in status epilepticus range from 42 to 95 percent across studies whose designs run from double-blind randomized trials to open-label trials and observational cohorts. Conventional meta-analysis treats that spread as statistical noise and pools without accounting for the systematic bias that open-label design, non-blinded outcome assessment and confounding introduce. The paper instead defines the ideal trial that would be run if resources and ethics allowed, evaluates how each study's design features depart from it, and models those features as covariates in meta-regression so that a target trial effect can be estimated for ideal conditions. A PRISMA-compliant search of five databases to November 2025 identified adult studies of first-line benzodiazepine monotherapy started out of hospital, with seizure cessation as the primary endpoint, excluding hospital-only settings because protocols, timing, drug availability and monitoring differ. Design features relevant to bias were extracted systematically. Traditional pooling was found to overstate efficacy by 3.9 percentage points attributable to open-label design, and network meta-analysis ranked intramuscular midazolam above intravenous lorazepam and diazepam. The proportion of heterogeneity attributable to design features rather than true variation was assessed.

future_research.gap: The magnitude of design-induced bias across studies of this question had not been quantified before.
future_research.quote: First, the magnitude of design-induced bias across studies has not been quantified.

problems.evidence: Rather than declaring studies concordant or not, the paper puts design features into a meta-regression and returns a bias magnitude on the outcome scale, 3.9 percentage points, plus a partition of heterogeneity into design-attributable and genuine. That is the calibrated comparison a binary replication verdict lacks, obtained here for one clinical question by assuming the design covariates capture the bias.
problems.quote: Traditional meta-analysis was found to overestimate benzodiazepine efficacy by 3.9 percentage points due to open-label design bias.

problems.evidence: The target trial here is a reference point for a whole evidence base rather than the design of one study, with every included study appraised against it and adjusted toward it. The adjustment is fitted within this set of studies on this question, so nothing carries the estimated design penalty to a different question or a different set of designs.
problems.quote: This approach defines a hypothetical target trial representing the ideal study one would conduct if resources and ethics permitted, then systematically evaluates how each study’s design features introduce bias relative to this target [ 9 – 13 ].

problems.evidence: The bias being estimated is attributable to design features that are recorded in a publication, blinding and design type, and the paper's premise is that conventional synthesis treats studies of very different assumption burden as exchangeable estimates. The design label is doing the work that an assumption assessment would, in both the conventional analysis being criticized and the correction being proposed.
problems.quote: Traditional meta-analytic approaches treat this heterogeneity as statistical noise, pooling estimates without accounting for systematic biases introduced by study design features.

papers.title: Target Trial Emulation Without Matching: A More Efficient Approach for Evaluating Vaccine Effectiveness Using Observational Data.
papers.one_line: Replaces matching in observational vaccine effectiveness studies with an explicitly defined estimand summarizing effectiveness over calendar time, identified under four stated assumptions and estimated from two hazard regressions, with substantial efficiency gains in COVID-19 vaccination among children aged 5 to 11.
papers.what_was_done: Emulation implies follow-up starts when an eligible person is vaccinated, which leaves no vaccination time for the unvaccinated, and the usual fix matches vaccinated to unvaccinated individuals on confounders and starts the pair's follow-up at the vaccinated member's vaccination date. The paper lists three problems with that: matching changes the target population, high-dimensional matching variables make matches hard to find and cost precision, and matching is usually done without articulating the estimand so its output is hard to interpret as a causal effect. An estimand is proposed that summarizes effectiveness over calendar time as vaccine efficacy is summarized in a trial, with identification resting on four stated assumptions including positivity of following the vaccine intervention within each covariate stratum on each day, no effect of intention to vaccinate and no vaccine effect until a lag of tau days, and equivalence between no vaccine on a given day and never vaccinating, since no placebo arm exists observationally. Two hazard regressions suffice for estimation. In simulation and in the Pfizer-BioNTech application the inferences agree with matching while the intervals are substantially narrower, and an R package is released.

future_research.gap: Vaccination timing may be driven by time-varying factors such as community transmission, which the method assumes away and would need more complex hazard formulations to accommodate.
future_research.quote:
First, we assume that baseline covariates measured at study start are sufficient to explain
vaccination timing. In practice, vaccination timing may be influenced by time-varying factors
such as community transmission levels.

future_research.gap: No interference is assumed and is unlikely to hold in infectious disease settings, though partial interference is thought feasible within the framework.
future_research.quote:
Another
shared limitation is our assumption of no interference, which may not hold in infectious disease
contexts.48,49

problems.evidence: The paper's central claim is that matching-based and sequential-trial vaccine studies are reported without a clear statement of what they estimate, and its contribution is to write the estimand down first and derive the estimator from it. The estimand it proposes is a calendar-time summary, chosen by analogy with how trial efficacy is summarized, so the ambiguity is resolved by a stated convention rather than by deriving what decision-makers need.
problems.quote:
By first articulating our causal
estimand, we were also able to develop a straight-forward and efficient estimation approach.21

problems.evidence: Two estimators for the same question are compared on efficiency in both simulation and application, with relative efficiency reported as a ratio of bootstrap variances, which is the demonstration that a choice mattered. The paper also reports that matching results depend on the random seed, so stable inference requires averaging over iterations, and that the proposed method avoids the bias-variance choice of which variables to match on.
problems.quote:
In addition, similar to others, we found that matching can depend on the
random seed set prior to matching.46,47

problems.evidence: The whole difficulty is that time zero is defined by an event only the treated experience, so the unvaccinated have no natural start of follow-up, and matching manufactures one by borrowing the vaccinated partner's date. The proposed alternative sets the origin at study start and handles timing through the hazard models, which replaces one convention with another and adds a lag parameter tau that must be specified.
problems.quote:
However, it is challenging to define “vaccination”
time for unvaccinated individuals.

problems.evidence: The control condition is defined as never vaccinating rather than receiving a placebo, because placebo vaccination is not observed in routine data, and no interference is assumed in a setting where one person's vaccination changes another's infection risk. The identified quantity therefore compares regimes whose joint implementation would change the transmission dynamics the estimate is conditioned on.
problems.quote: Assumption 4 emphasizes that we have defined the control intervention as “no vaccine” rather than placebo vaccine since placebo/control vaccines are not observed in observational data.

problems.evidence: Positivity here is a daily condition: within each covariate stratum on each of K days there must be a positive probability of following the vaccine intervention. That is far stronger than a single baseline overlap requirement and no diagnostic is offered for it, in a setting where uptake is concentrated in campaign periods and varies sharply by stratum.
problems.quote: Assumption 2 states that on each day, there is a positive probability that an individual follows the vaccine intervention of interest within each covariate strata.

papers.title: R WE ready for reimbursement? A round-up of developments in real-world evidence relating to health technology assessment: part 25.
papers.one_line: Reviews four emulations of GLP-1 receptor agonists and dementia against the failed phase III EVOKE trials of semaglutide in Alzheimer's disease, and shows the effect sizes track the comparator chosen while the observational and trial questions differ fundamentally.
papers.what_was_done: Three strands are covered. The first is a systematic analysis of how real-world data entered 147 French cost-effectiveness assessments between 2016 and 2023, with 88 percent incorporating at least one study, 527 studies in all, used mainly to characterize the population, validate models externally and describe comparators, and with about 8 percent of submissions invalidated for major methodological limitations such as external control arms. The second is a set of studies of GLP-1 receptor agonists and dementia. A TriNetX emulation across 113 million patients found semaglutide associated with 40 to 70 percent reductions in first Alzheimer's diagnosis, with hazard ratios of 0.33 against insulin, 0.31 against sulfonylureas and 0.59 against other GLP-1 agonists, and Kaplan-Meier curves separating within 30 days. A OneFlorida emulation found a 33 percent reduction against other second-line agents while SGLT2 inhibitors, acting by a different mechanism, showed a comparable or greater reduction with no difference between classes. A Medicare analysis using DPP-4 inhibitors as active comparator found no clear difference, risk ratio 0.83. The third is that Novo Nordisk stated the Alzheimer's programme was based on real-world evidence, and the EVOKE trials in 3,808 patients failed.

future_research.gap: Whether GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce dementia incidence in at-risk populations, the question the observational studies actually addressed, remains unanswered by the failed trials.
future_research.quote: The question of whether semaglutide or other GLP-1 receptor agonists might reduce the incidence of dementia in at-risk populations – the question actually addressed by the observational studies – remains open.

problems.evidence: A trial and a body of emulations disagreed, and the review's first explanation is that they answered different questions: incident dementia prevention in diabetic populations against slowing progression in biomarker-confirmed early Alzheimer's. Nothing established that mismatch before a phase III programme was launched on the strength of the observational evidence, and no procedure separates estimand mismatch from bias after the fact.
problems.quote: In the semaglutide–dementia literature, several of the studies were methodologically well-designed within the constraints of their data, but the fundamental question being answered – prevention of incident dementia diagnosis in diabetic populations – was different from the question posed by the EVOKE trial – slowing of progression in established, biomarker-confirmed AD.

problems.evidence: The effect size is a function of the comparator: largest against insulin and sulfonylureas, which mark advanced disease, smallest against other agents of the same class, and null against DPP-4 inhibitors. That gradient is what confounding by indication looks like, and each of these studies reports its own comparator's result as the effect of the drug.
problems.quote: Second, the choice of comparator in the observational studies profoundly influences the magnitude of the observed associations. Studies comparing GLP-1 receptor agonists against insulin or sulfonylureas reported the largest reductions. When DPP4 was the comparator, the overall effect was attenuated to non-significance.

problems.evidence: All the studies reviewed used the framework and reached opposite conclusions, and the review's own quality signal for the most credible one is transparency of specification rather than any property of the estimate. It states plainly that the framework cannot overcome unmeasured confounding, incomplete capture or outcome misclassification, so the label carries no information about those.
problems.quote: TTE is a valuable methodological approach, but it cannot overcome data-inherent biases arising from unmeasured confounding, incomplete variable capture, or outcome misclassification.

problems.evidence: Two independent signals of residual confounding are visible in these studies and neither is a formal diagnostic: survival curves separating within 30 days of initiation, and a drug acting by an entirely different mechanism showing an equal or larger apparent benefit. Both are read off the published figures by a commentator rather than produced by any check the studies ran.
problems.quote: The finding that SGLT2 inhibitors – which act through an entirely different mechanism – showed a similar or even greater apparent reduction in dementia risk raises important questions about whether the observed associations reflect a genuine neuroprotective drug effect or are instead driven by shared confounding factors.

problems.evidence: Roughly 8 percent of cost-effectiveness submissions containing real-world data were invalidated for major methodological limitations, which is a decision threshold being applied without a published standard, and the assessment body's own recommendations are for a standardized typology and a transparent framework that do not yet exist.
problems.quote: Approximately 8% of CEAs including RWD were invalidated due to major methodological limitations, such as the use of ECAs from RWD.

papers.title: REACT (Real-world Emulated Clinical Trials): A Framework for Drug Repurposing Applied to Osteoporotic Fractures.
papers.one_line: Screens 1,222 drugs for effects on osteoporotic fracture in claims data through an automated comparator-robust emulation pipeline, returns 18 with significant associations, and validates the output by whether the hits agree with existing biological and epidemiologic literature.
papers.what_was_done: Osteoporotic fractures affect around one in two women and one in four men over 50 in the United States, existing therapies carry adherence problems and rare serious harms, and few new agents are in development, so repurposing is proposed. REACT operationalizes target trial principles into an automated pipeline for high-throughput screening, applied to fracture prevention in older adults with osteoporosis. Screening 1,222 drugs returned 18 with statistically significant associations, 11 protective and 7 risk-increasing. The protective set includes angiotensin receptor blockers, statins, montelukast and spironolactone, each matched in the discussion to a published mechanism or prior epidemiologic finding, and the risk-increasing set is interpreted through falls and impaired mobility. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was used for confounding. The claims data lack bone mineral density, frailty assessment and imaging, exposure misclassification is possible, and the population is commercially insured United States adults aged 65 and over. The paper states the findings are exploratory signals requiring validation in independent datasets and prospective designs, and lists negative control outcome analyses, quantitative sensitivity analysis, cumulative exposure modeling, duration-stratified analyses and time-varying exposures as extensions not implemented.

future_research.gap: Formal negative control outcome analyses and quantitative sensitivity analyses for unmeasured confounding were not performed and would be needed to strengthen causal interpretation.
future_research.quote: Future research may incorporate formal negative control outcome analyses and quantitative sensitivity analyses for unmeasured confounding to further strengthen causal interpretation.

future_research.gap: Cumulative exposure, duration stratification and time-varying exposure are named as needed extensions and are absent from the current pipeline.
future_research.quote: Additional methodological extensions may include cumulative exposure modeling, duration-stratified analyses, time-varying exposures, integration of EHR-derived phenotypes, and external validation through prospective or pragmatic trial designs.

problems.evidence: The validation argument is that the pipeline's hits agree with what the literature already reports, which cannot distinguish a method that recovers true effects from one that reproduces the same confounding the prior literature carried. The paper calls this strong external validation while its own limitation section states the results are exploratory signals needing independent validation.
problems.quote: The recovery of mechanistically coherent protective drug classes—supported by established biological pathways 24 , 33 and prior epidemiologic evidence for beneficial effects on bone health 23 , 34 —provides strong external validation of the framework’s ability to surface clinically meaningful, literature-consistent signals rather than spurious associations.

problems.evidence: The clinical variables that determine fracture risk, bone mineral density, frailty and imaging, are absent from claims, so the eligibility condition and the confounding adjustment both run on billing proxies. Exposure misclassification is stated as possible with no quantification, across a screen of 1,222 drugs where a small systematic error would move which agents cross significance.
problems.quote: Claims data lack granular clinical measures such as bone mineral density, frailty assessments, and DXA imaging, and exposure misclassification remains possible.

problems.evidence: A screen of over a thousand drugs is run with weighting alone, and negative control outcomes and quantitative bias analysis are listed as future work. In a high-throughput setting the number of comparisons is exactly what makes an unmeasured-confounding check necessary, since confounding by frailty would act on many drugs at once and would look like a coherent signal.
problems.quote: Although IPTW reduces confounding, unmeasured bias may persist, and generalizability may be limited to commercially insured U.S. adults aged ≥65 years.

problems.evidence: Drugs are screened as exposures without cumulative dose, duration or time-varying use, which the paper lists as needed extensions. For agents whose bone effects are expected to depend on how long they are taken, such as statins and antiresorptives, an ever-versus-never contrast is not the strategy the biological hypothesis concerns.
problems.quote: At the same time, these findings should be interpreted as exploratory signals rather than definitive clinical recommendations.

papers.title: Trial emulation for validating the clinical efficacy of a foundational AI model in embryo selection.
papers.one_line: Uses target trial emulation with propensity matching across 4,674 embryos at two centres to move an AI embryo score from correlational validation to an estimated average treatment effect on implantation failure, while the intervention is a score rather than an action and the endpoint is a surrogate for live birth.
papers.what_was_done: Deep learning models for embryo selection are usually validated on discrimination metrics such as area under the curve, which ignore the confounders governing which embryo gets transferred, chiefly maternal age. An emulation framework was applied to FEMI, a foundational model trained by self-supervision on 18 million images, using 2,666 embryos from Weill Cornell between 2022 and 2024 and 2,008 from IVI Valencia between 2015 and 2019. Propensity score matching on patient and cycle covariates gave an average treatment effect of a high-risk ploidy score on implantation of minus 0.131 in the development cohort and minus 0.157 externally. S-learner individual treatment effect models showed the FEMI score carried a stronger effect than the manual blastocyst score, minus 0.103 against minus 0.092, and 47.7 and 38.9 percent stronger than two commercial AI scores externally, with superiority surviving age-adjusted composite comparators. The paper concludes this provides pre-clinical justification for a randomized trial. The endpoint is implantation rather than live birth, the individual-effect analysis does not simulate ranking a patient's whole embryo cohort, and sperm quality, stimulation protocol and patient genetics are unmeasured.

future_research.gap: The analysis does not reproduce the actual clinical decision, which is ranking all of one patient's embryos to pick one, and prospective designs would be needed to evaluate that.
future_research.quote: Secondly, while our ITE analysis demonstrates per-embryo predictive superiority, it does not fully simulate the clinical decision process of ranking an entire cohort for a single patient.

future_research.gap: Predicting live birth rather than implantation will need multimodal models combining image scores with maternal clinical variables.
future_research.quote: Future efforts to predict live birth probabilities with high precision will require multimodal models that integrate FEMI’s image-based scores with comprehensive maternal clinical variables.

problems.evidence: The exposure is a model output rather than an action anyone takes: a high-risk score is contrasted with a low-risk score among embryos that were all transferred. No treatment strategy is specified that a clinic could follow, and the clinical use the paper envisages, ranking a patient's embryos and transferring the best, is a different intervention that the design does not evaluate.
problems.quote: By using propensity score matching, we successfully created balanced treatment and control groups, isolating the effect of the FEMI-Ploidy score from patient and cycle covariates.

problems.evidence: Implantation stands in for live birth, and the paper states that progression to live birth depends on downstream factors extrinsic to the embryo that imaging cannot capture. The events that determine whether the surrogate translates are exactly the ones the design cannot observe, and the surrogate is the endpoint on which the case for a randomized trial rests.
problems.quote: Finally, our primary clinical endpoint was implantation. While this is a strong and direct surrogate for embryo viability, live birth rate remains the ultimate clinical goal.

problems.evidence: Propensity matching on measured patient and cycle covariates is presented as converting a correlational score into a causally relevant predictor, while the paper acknowledges residual confounding from sperm quality, stimulation protocol and patient genetics. The flexible model and the matching step together are being read as identification, and the unmeasured factors are ones that plausibly drive both which embryo is chosen and whether it implants.
problems.quote: The resulting significant ATE confirms that a high-risk FEMI score is not just a correlate of a poor-quality embryo, but a causally relevant predictor of implantation failure (ATE = −0.131) in the WCM cohort.

problems.evidence: The two cohorts differ in country, in years covered, 2022 to 2024 against 2015 to 2019, in median maternal age, and in laboratory practice and equipment, and the paper states these could independently influence implantation rates in ways matching did not capture. The external cohort is used as validation and as the site where the effect is largest.
problems.quote: Inherent differences in baseline demographics (e.g., a significantly lower median maternal age in the Spain cohort) and center-specific laboratory practices or equipment could independently influence implantation rates, introducing heterogeneity not fully captured by the matched variables.

papers.title: Target trial emulation: bridging observational studies and randomized trials for health decision-making.
papers.one_line: Reviews the framework for decision-makers and proposes living protocols on continuously updated registry data, while noting that multiple defensible choices exist at each protocol component and that existing reporting standards do not capture what an emulation must report.
papers.what_was_done: The review sets out three steps: formulate a precise causal question, specify the target trial protocol explicitly, and replicate each component in observational data, with propensity matching, weighting, g-methods and instrumental variables as the analytic toolkit. Positivity is stated with its violation modes, subgroups deterministically assigned to a treatment by clinical guidelines, contraindications or structural features of the health system, and the consequence that causal contrasts cannot be estimated for those subgroups. Two published protocols are examined, one on special educational needs provision and one on emergency surgery, and the review notes that in the latter clone-censor-weighting could have been used instead for the seven-day grace period and different strategies could have addressed unmeasured confounding. Missing data is treated as pervasive across confounders, exposure timing and dosage, and outcomes when patients move between care settings, with a prespecified strategy recommended to prevent post hoc adjustment and selective reporting. STROBE and RECORD are stated not to cover the specific requirements of emulation, which the 21-item TARGET checklist addresses. Registry data that update continuously are proposed to support living protocols refined as data accumulate.

future_research.gap: Prospective-retrospective hybrid designs using continuously updated registries are proposed as an evolution that does not yet exist in practice.
future_research.quote: Registry-based TTE frameworks introduce the concept of ‘living protocols,’ where study designs evolve as registry data are continuously updated.

problems.evidence: The review points at a published protocol and observes that a different method could have handled its grace period and different strategies could have addressed its unmeasured confounding. Its answer is that stating the protocol makes the choices visible, which converts an absence of criteria into a transparency requirement and leaves alternative analyses to future work.
problems.quote: For example, in the ESORT study, alternative approaches such as clone-censor-weighting could have been used to handle the 7-day grace period, and different strategies could address unmeasured confounding.

problems.evidence: Positivity is stated in a form specific to emulation, that every strategy in the protocol must be empirically represented, and its violations are attributed to identifiable structural causes rather than to sampling: guidelines, contraindications and how the health system is organized. The consequence is drawn correctly, that contrasts are unestimable for those subgroups, without offering a diagnostic that names them.
problems.quote: Violations of positivity may occur when certain subgroups are deterministically assigned to a specific treatment due to clinical guidelines, contraindications or structural features of the healthcare system. Without positivity, causal contrasts cannot be estimated for subgroups of the population.

problems.evidence: Living protocols that evolve as registry data accumulate are proposed as an advance, and the same review warns that a missing data strategy must be prespecified to prevent post hoc adjustment and selective reporting. A protocol that is revised as data arrive is in tension with the prespecification that gives the framework its discipline, and the review does not address what constrains the revisions.
problems.quote: Notably, TTE frameworks utilizing continuously updated registry data enable ‘living protocols’ that can be iteratively refined as new data accumulate, representing an important evolution toward prospective-retrospective hybrid designs that maintain causal clarity while addressing emerging clinical questions.

problems.evidence: The review states that existing observational reporting frameworks do not capture what an emulation requires and that inconsistent reporting of eligibility, strategies, follow-up, outcomes, estimands and analytic choices is a major current limitation, then points to a 21-item checklist that addresses it. The checklist covers specification and mapping rather than distinguishing which of the resulting assumptions can be checked against data.
problems.quote: Existing observational study reporting frameworks, such as STROBE and RECORD, do not fully capture the specific requirements of TTE.

papers.title: Transferability of Real World Evidence to Support HTA Recommendations in Lower Income European Countries.
papers.one_line: Works through whether an emulation of erythropoiesis-stimulating agents in myelodysplastic syndrome, built from a European registry covering 18 countries and no lower-income ones, can inform reimbursement decisions in countries the registry does not cover.
papers.what_was_done: Lower income European countries have less capacity to fund high-cost rare disease technologies and less capacity to conduct health technology assessment, so the opportunity cost of a wrong decision is larger there while methods development happens elsewhere. The paper notes that European projects advancing assessment methods under-represent Eastern European member states and may therefore widen the gap between early and late adopters. Myelodysplastic syndrome was chosen because diagnostic uncertainty, patient safety and ethics limit randomized testing and existing trials are small, selective and inaccessible, so a target trial was emulated in the European Myelodysplastic Syndromes Registry to estimate the causal average effect of erythropoiesis-stimulating agents against none in lower-risk patients. The registry covers 18 countries and includes no lower income ones. Assessment agency partners set expectations for integrating the method into routine work, and workshops with consortium members and external experts identified barriers. The absence of local real-world data before a reimbursement decision emerged as the principal obstacle, alongside differences in patient pathways and comparator technologies and limited expertise and resources for adapting international methods. Five concluding statements were produced.

future_research.gap: How real-world evidence generated by emulation in higher income settings can be transferred to countries with limited assessment capacity had not been explored before this study.
future_research.quote: This is the first study to explore how RWE generated by the TTE method can be transferred to optimize treatment decisions of patients with a rare disease in countries with limited HTA capacities.

problems.evidence: The estimate must travel from a registry covering 18 countries, none of them the ones that need it, into settings where the patient pathway and the available comparators are different. Those two differences change the treatment strategies being contrasted rather than only the covariate distribution, and the paper lists them as barriers rather than as quantities any transport method addresses.
problems.quote: Differences in patient pathways and comparator technologies, limited expertise and resources for adapting international HTA methods are significant barriers of transferring RWE from other countries.

problems.evidence: The stated principal obstacle is that the countries making the decision have no local real-world data at the time they make it, so the fitness question cannot even be asked of a source they do not have. The registry that does exist is described as needing detailed information on patients, disease and treatment for the analysis to work, which is a requirement stated without a threshold.
problems.quote: The lack of local real‐world data before making reimbursement decisions is an important challenge to apply the TTE method to LIECs.

problems.evidence: The exercise is aimed at getting an emulation accepted by reimbursement bodies, and what it produced is five concluding statements developed through workshops rather than any criterion an agency could apply. Agencies set expectations for the case study team, which locates the standard in a negotiation rather than in a published threshold.
problems.quote: HTA agency consortium partners set expectations for the MDS case study team on how to integrate the new TTE methodology into the routine work of HTA bodies.

problems.evidence: The paper describes as a novel feature that each subject can be enrolled in every target trial for which they are eligible, and presents it as an analytic convenience without noting that the same person then contributes to multiple trials. In a rare disease registry with few patients that repeated participation is the mechanism by which the design gains its power.
problems.quote: A novel aspect of target trial methodology is that, for purposes of data analysis, each subject in the observational study can be enrolled in all target trials for which the subject is eligible, instead of a single trial.

papers.title: Target Trial Emulation to Incorporate Real-World Data in the Estimation of the Clinical and Cost-Effectiveness of Biologic Treatment.
papers.one_line: Emulates a trial of rituximab against non-biologic therapy after first-line biologic failure in a rheumatoid arthritis register, feeds the response probabilities into an economic model, and moves the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio from about 34,700 to 46,800 pounds per quality-adjusted life-year.
papers.what_was_done: Randomized evidence on biologic effectiveness after first-line failure is limited, so cost-effectiveness analysis of the treatment pathway relies on assuming the first-line effect generalizes or on non-randomized sources. A target trial was specified and emulated in the British Society for Rheumatology Biologics Register, estimating the effect of rituximab against non-biologic therapy on achieving a European response category, with inverse probability of treatment weighting for measured baseline differences. Rituximab gave probabilities of 0.215 for a moderate or good response and 0.090 for a good response against 0.174 and 0.066 for the comparator, well below the 0.650 and 0.150 estimated from trial data. Pooled with trial estimates in a meta-analysis and entered into the economic model, this produced less time on treatment, lower costs, 63,500 against 70,000 pounds, and a higher cost-effectiveness ratio. The target trial was specified as a pragmatic trial in which participants know their assignment, so no placebo effect could be accounted for. Disease activity is recorded at appointments roughly every six months and those dates did not coincide with the treatment changes defining baseline and follow-up, so the closest visits were used.

future_research.gap: Why real-world and trial effect estimates differ for these treatments was not explored and would need investigation of population and setting differences.
future_research.quote: Although we did not explore the reasons for the discrepancy, future work could investigate how differences in the RCT and RWD populations/settings influence the differences in effect estimates obtained from each evidence source.

future_research.gap: Methods for synthesizing real-world and randomized evidence on effectiveness while accounting for the strengths and limitations of each source need further development.
future_research.quote: Further development of evidence synthesis methods for combining RWD and RCT data on treatment effectiveness, while accounting for the strengths and limitations of each evidence source, would also be useful.

problems.evidence: The outcome is a change in disease activity between baseline and follow-up, and the register measures disease activity every six months on a schedule unrelated to when treatment changed. The paper works out the direction of the resulting bias: a measurement taken after treatment started misses the initial response, so the change is underestimated and the effect is biased downward.
problems.quote: For example, where the DAS28 is measured after the start of the treatment, it may not truly represent the initial reduction in disease activity due to the treatment response. Thus, the change in disease activity from baseline to follow-up will be underestimated, which will bias the treatment effect toward lower values.

problems.evidence: The real-world response probability is a third of the trial's, 0.215 against 0.650, and the paper attributes this to population differences without decomposing it. Those two numbers are then pooled in a meta-analysis and the pooled value drives a cost-effectiveness ratio, so an unexplained factor-of-three discrepancy is resolved by averaging.
problems.quote: The EULAR response probabilities associated with second-line RTX estimated in our TTE analysis were much lower than those based on RCT data (see Table 4 ).

problems.evidence: The target trial was specified as pragmatic with participants aware of their assignment, and the outcome is a partly patient-reported disease activity score. The paper states this means no placebo effect can be accounted for and the effect is likely overestimated, so the estimand includes a component the trial estimates it is compared against explicitly exclude.
problems.quote: We defined a target trial protocol for a pragmatic RCT in which participants were aware of their assigned treatment. Therefore, we could not account for a placebo effect in our analysis, and this is likely to have led to an overestimate of the treatment effect because individuals are prone to score better on patient-reported outcomes (e.g., pain) when aware of their treatment.

problems.evidence: The comparator arm contains a higher proportion of patients who cannot take a biologic because of contraindication, and the treated arm a higher proportion who stopped previous biologic therapy for inefficacy, 60.6 against 44.5 percent. Adjusting for the latter is stated as possibly not sufficient, and the former is a structural reason the two arms are not exchangeable.
problems.quote: Although we adjusted for the difference in the proportion of individuals who stopped previous biologic therapy due to inefficacy between the 2 treatment groups, this may not have completely mitigated this selection bias.

problems.evidence: The evidence feeding a reimbursement decision was neither graded nor formally assessed, with the analysis assuming weighting was sufficient to handle confounding. A cost-effectiveness ratio that moves by 12,000 pounds per quality-adjusted life-year depending on the evidence source is produced without any threshold governing whether that source is adequate.
problems.quote: We did not grade the quality of evidence from the register and assumed that the aforementioned techniques were sufficient to mitigate confounding.

papers.title: The Ideal Trial: Defining Causal Estimands that Balance Relevance and Feasibility in Target Trial Emulations and Actual Randomized Trials.
papers.one_line: Argues that specifying a target trial aligned with the observational data at hand, the standard recommendation, produces an estimand that may not answer the decision question, and proposes the ideal trial as the common reference against which both emulations and actual trials should be appraised.
papers.what_was_done: A causal estimand can be defined mathematically or, equivalently, by specifying an ideal trial: a hypothetical perfect randomized experiment with a representative sample and perfect adherence. The paper reviews both routes, shows their equivalence, and argues that either way the definition requires balancing practical relevance against feasibility of estimation. It then examines the aligned approach to target trial specification, in which the target trial is written to match the data, for instance by adopting the data's own eligibility criteria, and which is both recommended and common in applications. Under that approach the emulation can be internally valid with respect to its target trial while remaining biased relative to the estimand of ultimate interest, and those residual biases mirror the ones actual trials carry and rarely address. The paper attributes this to overemphasis on internal validity, with non-representativeness relegated to external validity and left unaddressed, and endorses appraising studies against overall target validity instead. A structured device is proposed: a table with the ideal trial in one column and the emulation or trial in others, functioning as a checklist for identifying every bias source, since limitations sections currently have none and are compiled haphazardly. An example from respiratory epidemiology illustrates.

future_research.gap: Studies bringing together multiple trials and observational studies should appraise each against a common ideal-trial reference rather than against one another, which is not current practice.
future_research.quote: Indeed, comparing one study with another is the usual practice, whereas in the logic of causal inference, each study should be appraised against a common reference, defined in terms of the causal estimand of ultimate interest (i.e., the ideal trial), as has been argued elsewhere. 42

problems.evidence: This is the missing separation named directly: the emulation may be unbiased relative to its specified target trial and still biased relative to the estimand of practical interest, and the paper argues that the claim a correct emulation removes everything but baseline confounding holds only relative to the target trial as specified. The proposed remedy is a side-by-side table of ideal trial against emulation acting as a checklist, which surfaces the sources without quantifying or apportioning them.
problems.quote: For instance, it has been suggested that a correct target trial emulation eliminates common sources of bias except possibly for baseline confounding, 9 but this is relative to the specified target trial and the study may still be subject to other important biases relative to the ideal trial.

problems.evidence: The aligned approach writes the target trial to fit the data, for example by adopting the data's eligibility criteria, so the trial that inference conditions on is a function of what was available rather than of the question. The paper's objection is exactly that this optimizes feasibility of estimation and can leave the estimand irrelevant to the decision it is meant to inform.
problems.quote: The main issue is that this approach puts the focus heavily on the feasibility of unbiased estimation with the available data, resulting in an estimand that may not be relevant to addressing the question of most interest to real-world decision-making.

problems.evidence: The paper observes that identifying a study's limitations has no checklist, so the process is haphazard and invites selective reporting, and offers the ideal-trial column as one. That is a structured device for enumerating assumption failures rather than a dashboard distinguishing the diagnosable from the undiagnosable.
problems.quote: In particular, although researchers invariably consider the limitations of their study in their interpretation, the process by which they identify and list these limitations (e.g., in the discussion of a manuscript) can be haphazard: there is no “checklist,” which can lead to selective consideration and reporting.

problems.evidence: Benchmarking an emulation against an actual trial compares two imperfect studies without a common reference, and the paper notes that a published harmonized protocol comparing a trial with an observational study used an aligned rather than an ideal protocol as its reference point. The index-trial practice of motivating a target trial from a real one is distinguished on the same ground, since an actual trial is itself imperfect.
problems.quote: This is similar in spirit to the harmonized protocol presented by Lodi et al., 43 who compared an actual trial and an observational study, but their reference point was an aligned rather than an ideal protocol.

problems.evidence: The paper names an overconfidence in evidence from emulations that parallels the acknowledged overconfidence in evidence from trials, and traces it to internal validity being treated as the whole of validity. A study described as a correct emulation carries a claim whose scope is set by its own target trial and not by the question anyone wants answered.
problems.quote: Understanding these assumptions is important to avoid an overconfidence in evidence arising from target trial emulations that mirrors the generally acknowledged overconfidence in evidence arising from actual trials. 39 , 40
